name: dsh
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 against DeepSeek Harness Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3 on Windows 11, from dsh's own installed documentation and sources plus a live session. (1) USER-GLOBAL RULES: dsh-agent-instructions composes the user-global chain as $DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md first, then <agentsHome>/AGENTS.md ($DSH_AGENTS_HOME or ~/.agents) — the standard preset mounts it with maxBytes 65536 — so .dsh/AGENTS.md is the managed target, and ~/.agents/AGENTS.md is the user-owned overlay slot for machine-specific additions (editing the managed file is what `apply` reverts). (2) SKILLS: ~/.agents/skills is a native user skill root; project .agents/skills overrides it and the packaged preset skill overrides both, so the same link pi uses is enough — this manifest declares no skill dimension on purpose. (3) PLUGINS: dsh does NOT auto-load an extensions directory; a row has to be mounted through the Cordis composition, which is why gates/commands declare auto_load false and carry a verified patch row. An installed plugin directory also needs package.json {"type":"module"} because these plugins are ES modules (bridge/lib/gates.js and bridge/lib/commands.js write it). (4) COMMANDS: dsh registers slash commands from plugins (`ctx.commands.register`), and ships no prompt-template directory, so Claude's command files are only reachable through the plugin this target installs (dsh/commands/), which copies them into prompts/*.md and injects one as the user's next prompt through `agent.followup()`. (5) MCP: dsh has NO global mcp.json equivalent — live servers are either the profile composition's `mcp-manager` row (a settings surface the GUI also writes) or registrations a plugin contributes at runtime. Rewriting the profile is off the table (never_touch), so this target splits the problem. `bridge apply` owns ONE generated document (~/.dsh/agent-config-bridge/mcp.json, Claude-shaped, mode 600 because entries may carry credentials), and `dsh/mcp/` is a reader plugin installed by `scripts/install-dsh.js --only mcp` that registers every entry with ctx.mcpManager.register() and reconciles on change — a running dsh therefore picks up a `bridge apply` without a restart. The reader needs one mount row (`auto_load: false`), and `/mcp` + `/mcp restart <name>` from the sibling commands plugin operate on exactly these registrations. Credentials stay literal in that document: Claude's .claude.json carries literal values and ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml is never_touch, so the `${credential:NAME}` template route mcp-manager supports would require writing the credentials store — refused on purpose.

managed.note: the fixed user-global instruction file dsh-agent-instructions loads first, before the shared agents root. Because `apply` owns this file, machine-specific DSH additions belong in ~/.agents/AGENTS.md (loaded second, never written by this project) rather than in edits here.

the prompt templates behind the installed slash-command plugin. dsh has no prompt-template directory: the plugin (dsh/commands/index.js) reads this directory at activation and registers one command per file, injecting the rendered template as the user's next prompt. Copied from ~/.claude/commands so the prompt text stays owned by the user and by Claude Code.

the document the installed reader (the mcp_reader block) feeds into dsh's mcp-manager at runtime. Claude-shaped on purpose: the reader — and a human debugging it — see the same fields the authoritative source has. mode 600 because it may carry expanded credentials.

gates.reason: Hard gates moved to ShipGate (assets/gates + `shipgate policy`). agent-config-bridge keeps only skills / commands / rules-doc / MCP.
